title: Medical and Life-Support Protections — Recertification, Expiration and Reactivation within the Grace Period
content:
A certification under Medical and Life-Support Protections runs to its expiration date. The rule on its renewal is as follows.

> A reminder is sent the protection's recertification notice period before the expiration date. A new practitioner form received while the certification is active extends the term to the new certified date plus the protection's certification term in months, less one day. Without one, the certification expires on the day after its expiration date. A late recertification reactivates an expired protection only within the recertification grace period after the expiration date. The grace period is counted in calendar days from the day after the expiration date, and a form received on the last day is in time. Protections do not apply during the lapse between expiration and reactivation.

The expiration date and the date the form is received are read from the company's record of the certification concerned.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Situation on the day the new practitioner form is received | Result |
|---|---|
| certification active | term extended to the new certified date plus the term in months, less one day; the new certified date, expiration date, practitioner license number and devices certified on the new form are recorded |
| certification expired, form received on or before the last day of the grace period | the protection is reactivated; the new certified date, the new last day of the term, the practitioner license number and the date of reactivation are recorded |
| certification expired, form received after the last day of the grace period | the late recertification does not reactivate the protection |

A certification with no new form received while active moves from active to expired on the day after its expiration date. One reminder is recorded per certification term, on the date it is sent; where the reminder period is 0, no reminder is sent.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

Expiration date 30 April; the certification is not renewed while active, so it expires on 1 May.

| Grace period | Day 1 | Last day | Form received | Reactivates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days | 1 May | 30 May | 30 May | yes |
| 30 days | 1 May | 30 May | 31 May | no |
| 45 days | 1 May | 14 June | 14 June | yes |
| 45 days | 1 May | 14 June | 15 June | no |

A grace period of 0 means there is none.

## The lapse

Between the expiration and the reactivation the protections do not apply. In the first row above, a form received on 30 May reactivates the protection, and the protections did not apply from 1 May until the reactivation.

## Extension while active (hypothetical)

A certification with a 12-month term and the expiration date 30 April receives a new practitioner form certified on 20 March, while it is still active. The term is extended to 20 March of the following year less one day, that is, to 19 March of the following year.
